title: The loss of Situational Awareness
excerpt: A bunch of supposedly smart people gave money to a first-time hedge fund adviser on the strength of his essay about AI. It didn’t go well!
content_html:
I am not by any means an expert at finance but I think I do now have some advice for people who are: Do not name your hedge fund anything that will be hilarious if it blows up. Don’t use a name like “Long-Term Capital Management” or “Amaranth Advisors” (named for the floral symbol for immortality). Certainly do not call yourself “Situational Awareness,” which might as well just be “Hubris, Inc.”

Anyway, Situational Awareness, the hedge fund started by a 24-year-old former OpenAI employee that focuses on artificial intelligence bets, has sold most or all, depending on who’s reporting, of its entire public stock portfolio to Ken Griffin’s Citadel after several bad weeks for AI stocks, and that’s the situation we are all now aware of. You may recall earlier this week I noted the market had gotten particularly nervous about AI risk; as it turns out, we have discovered one firm that was swimming without a bathing suit.

How bad is it? Well, according to CNBC, the fund was worth $45 billion at the start of July. It is now worth $10 billion, after the sale of assets to Griffin. The previous record holder on all-time trading losses was Archegos Capital Management, which lost $8 billion in 10 days in 2021, according to The Wall Street Journal. If these numbers hold, Situational Awareness’ AI bets lost three times as much.

Every detail of this disaster is funnier than the last. Situational Awareness had a staff of eight, of whom four were investment professionals. “The fund’s largest holdings at the end of the first quarter included Nebius Group, Sandisk, Micron and CoreWeave, according to filings,” CNBC wrote. “All four of those stocks are down more than 35 percent this month.” I expect we will hear more in the coming days, especially from the Wall Street professionals who were on the other side of these jokers’ trades.

“Basically, this investment firm will be kind of like a brain trust on AI.”

How did we get here? Situational Awareness LP was named for a series of facile essays about machine intelligence published by the improbably named Leopold Aschenbrenner, the 24-year-old mastermind of the hedge fund. “We are building machines that can think and reason,” he writes, betraying that he has no idea what thinking could possibly mean. “By 2025/26, these machines will outpace many college graduates. By the end of the decade, they will be smarter than you or I; we will have superintelligence, in the true sense of the word. Along the way, national security forces not seen in half a century will be unleashed, and before long, The Project will be on. If we’re lucky, we’ll be in an all-out race with the CCP; if we’re unlucky, an all-out war.”

There is a part of me that wants to go line by line to dunk on every claim here, beginning with the very first sentence, “You can see the future first in San Francisco,” but I am going to stifle the impulse. The essays are the theoretical underpinnings of the hedge fund. The upshot is that artificial general intelligence is real (lol) and will arrive in 2027 (lmao). So the entire point of the hedge fund was to dump as much money as possible into AI stocks and then get very, very rich.

“Basically, this investment firm will be kind of like a brain trust on AI,” Aschenbrenner told Dwarkesh Patel in a four-hour podcast interview, the preferred intellectual medium of the Silicon Valley elite. “We’re going to have way more situational awareness than any of the people who manage money in New York. We’re definitely going to do great on investing, but it’s the same sort of situational awareness that is going to be important for understanding what’s happening, being a voice of reason publicly, and being able to be in a position to advise.”

I really cannot begin to explain how much this essay’s bad graphs impressed A Certain Kind of Silicon Valley Guy. Axios wrote breathlessly about the essay that “his opus is a useful, eye-opening synthesis of high-level Silicon Valley conversations.” Aschenbrenner’s insights “expanded my perspective as an AI practitioner beyond just the technical aspects,” wrote Shav Vimalendiran, a cofounder of SAMMY Labs, an AI company that is meant to simplify legal statutes. You know who else liked it? Ivanka Trump, who called it “an excellent and important read.”

Why would these purportedly serious people buy in on a 24-year-old’s very first hedge fund?

Situational Awareness’ backers included Patrick and John Collison, who cofounded Stripe, and two Meta AI leaders, Daniel Gross and Nat Friedman. The fund’s director of research was Carl Shulman, who’d worked at Peter Thiel’s Clarium Capital. Eventually, Jane Street — the Wall Street firm budding young Effective Altruists, including Sam Bankman-Fried, join — bought in too. “Jane Street’s investment in Situational Awareness is particularly notable because the firm rarely allocates capital to outside money managers,” The Wall Street Journal wrote in June.

Why would these purportedly serious people buy in on a 24-year-old’s very first hedge fund? My best guess is that Aschenbrenner’s investors were relying on the social bona fides he had cultivated. Social proof is the laziest and most disastrous way to vet people — ask any Theranos investor, or for that matter, anyone who had Bernie Madoff managing their money — but I suppose it’s good enough for Silicon Valley.

At age 17, Aschenbrenner was called “an economics prodigy” by Tyler Cowen, a libertarian economist famous in certain Silicon Valley circles. Cowen’s Emergent Ventures even gave him a grant, according to Fortune. Aschenbrenner published essays in Works in Progress, a publication funded by Stripe. During his time at Columbia University, Aschenbrenner cofounded the college’s Effective Altruism chapter. After graduating in 2021 as Columbia University’s valedictorian at age 19, Aschenbrenner went on to work at the FTX Future Fund, the philanthropic arm of cryptocurrency exchange FTX, which collapsed after Sam Bankman-Fried’s fraud was revealed. Among his coworkers at the fund were William MacAskill, the philosopher-king of the Effective Altruism movement, and Avital Balwit, who would later become the chief of staff at Anthropic.

From there, he immediately got a job on OpenAI’s superalignment team. Fortune quotes several former coworkers who describe him as being “politically clumsy,” arrogant, and abrasive. “Multiple researchers also described a holiday party where, in a casual group discussion, Aschenbrenner told then Scale AI CEO Alexandr Wang how many GPUs OpenAI had—‘just straight out in the open,’ as one put it,” wrote Fortune’s Sharon Goldman in her profile. (Both Wang and Aschenbrenner deny this occurred.) Aschenbrenner was later fired from OpenAI for leaking internal information in an incident unrelated to the Scale AI thing. Two months after that, Aschenbrenner published Situational Awareness, his essays.

“Obviously, not blowing up is task number one and two.”

Now astute readers may notice that Aschenbrenner had no previous money management experience on his resume when he launched his hedge fund. They may also notice that the sum total of Aschenbrenner’s work experience was a few months at FTX and about a year at OpenAI. They may wonder if this means that the Collisons, Gross, and Friedman have too much money to burn if they are funding this little shit. (Yes, obviously. Tax the rich!)

Here’s how Aschenbrenner described the fund’s strategy back in the halcyon days of 2024: “Obviously, not blowing up is task number one and two,” he told Patel. “You have to get the timing right. The sequence of bets on the way to AGI is actually pretty critical. People underrate it.”

We’ll get a more complete picture of how Situational Awareness crashed and burned in the coming days, but right now it looks like this. Hedge funds often borrow money to maximize their bets. So if you really believe AI is the future, “you won’t put 100% of your money (and your investors’ money) into the AI boom,” writes Bloomberg’s Matt Levine. “You’ll put, like, 300% of your money into the AI boom.” At one point, the hedge fund claimed to be up 439 percent.

The same borrowing that magnifies your wins also magnifies your losses. If you have borrowed money to bet on AI stocks, and those stocks go down — as they have done recently — the people you borrowed from will do what’s called a “margin call” and ask you to top up your loan collateral. First, Situational Awareness held calls with its investors and lenders to raise more capital, The Financial Times reported yesterday. It even offered some investors the opportunity to buy parts of its portfolio. This morning, Situational Awareness sold what the FT said was “a large portion of its $16bn public equity” to Citadel, Griffin’s hedge fund.

“You’ve got to be really, really careful about your overall risk positioning.”

Public equity is the most liquid part of anyone’s portfolio. Situational Awareness still has private holdings, including $5 billion in Anthropic, the FT reported. According to CNBC, Situational Awareness was also negotiating to sell that stake, “but it wasn’t clear if that deal was done.”

“You’ve got to be really, really careful about your overall risk positioning,” Aschenbrenner said in 2024. “If you expect these crazy events to play out, there’s going to be crazy things you didn’t foresee.” One of those things, perhaps, is that artificial general intelligence isn’t coming — or at least, not by 2027. “A friend joked that the investment firm is perfectly hedged for me,” Aschenbrenner said. “Either AGI happens this decade and my human capital depreciates, but I turn it into financial capital, or no AGI happens and the firm doesn’t do well, but I’m still in my twenties and smart.”

Yes, Aschenbrenner is certainly in his 20s!

sentences.en: Elizabeth Lopatto

content_html_zh:
我无论如何都不是金融方面的专家，但我想我现在确实对那些人有一些建议：不要为你的对冲基金命名任何如果它爆炸的话会很搞笑的名字。 不要使用“长期资本管理”或“苋菜顾问”（以代表不朽的花卉符号命名）之类的名称。 当然，不要称自己为“态势感知”，这还不如“Hubris, Inc.”。

无论如何，Situational Awareness 这家由 24 岁的 OpenAI 前员工创立的对冲基金专注于人工智能押注，在人工智能股票经历了几周的糟糕表现后，它已经将其整个公开股票投资组合的大部分或全部出售给 Ken Griffin 的 Citadel，这取决于报告者，这就是我们现在都知道的情况。 你可能还记得本周早些时候我指出市场对人工智能风险特别紧张；事实证明，我们发现一家公司在没有穿泳衣的情况下游泳。

有多糟糕？ 据 CNBC 报道，截至 7 月初，该基金的价值为 450 亿美元。 在将资产出售给格里芬后，该公司目前价值 100 亿美元。 据《华尔街日报》报道，此前历史交易亏损纪录保持者是 Archegos Capital Management，该公司在 2021 年 10 天内亏损了 80 亿美元。 如果这些数字成立，态势感知公司的人工智能赌注损失将是原来的三倍。

这场灾难的每一个细节都比上一场更有趣。 态势感知部门有八名员工，其中四名是投资专业人士。 CNBC 写道：“根据文件，该基金第一季度末最大的持股包括 Nebius Group、Sandisk、Micron 和 CoreWeave。” “这四只股票本月均下跌超过 35%。” 我预计未来几天我们会听到更多消息，尤其是来自这些小丑交易另一边的华尔街专业人士的消息。

“基本上，这家投资公司有点像人工智能的智囊团。”

我们是怎么到这里的？ Situational Awareness LP 得名于一系列关于机器智能的浅显文章，这些文章的作者是 24 岁的对冲基金策划者利奥波德·阿申布伦纳 (Leopold Aschenbrenner)，他的名字令人难以置信。 “我们正在建造能够思考和推理的机器，”他写道，这表明他不知道思考可能意味着什么。 “到 2025/26 年，这些机器的速度将超过许多大学毕业生。 到本世纪末，他们将比你我更聪明；我们将拥有真正意义上的超级智能。 在此过程中，半个世纪未见的国家安全力量将被释放，不久之后，该项目将开始。 运气好的话，我们会和中共进行一场全力以赴的比赛；如果我们运气不好的话，就会爆发全面战争。”

我内心有一部分想要逐行地对这里的每一个主张进行扣篮，从第一句话开始，“你可以在旧金山首先看到未来”，但我要抑制这种冲动。 这些文章是对冲基金的理论基础。 结果是，通用人工智能是真实存在的（笑），并将在 2027 年到来（lmao）。 因此，对冲基金的全部意义就是将尽可能多的资金投入人工智能股票，然后变得非常非常富有。

“基本上，这家投资公司将有点像人工智能的智囊团，”阿申布伦纳在四小时的播客采访中告诉德瓦克什·帕特尔，播客是硅谷精英首选的智力媒介。 “我们将比纽约任何管理资金的人拥有更多的态势感知能力。 我们肯定会在投资方面做得很好，但同样的态势感知对于了解正在发生的事情、公开发出理性的声音以及能够提供建议也很重要。”

我真的无法解释这篇文章中糟糕的图表给某类硅谷人留下了多么深刻的印象。 Axios 气喘吁吁地评论这篇文章，“他的作品是硅谷高层对话的有用、令人大开眼界的综合。” SAMMY Labs 是一家致力于简化法律法规的人工智能公司，其联合创始人 Shav Vimalendiran 写道，Aschenbrenner 的见解“拓展了我作为人工智能从业者的视野，超越了技术层面”。 你知道还有谁喜欢它吗？ 伊万卡·特朗普 (Ivanka Trump) 称其为“一本出色且重要的读物”。

为什么这些自称严肃​​的人会购买一个 24 岁年轻人的第一支对冲基金？

Situational Awareness 的支持者包括 Stripe 联合创始人 Patrick 和 John Collison，以及两位 Meta AI 领导者 Daniel Gross 和 Nat Friedman。 该基金的研究主管是卡尔·舒尔曼 (Carl Shulman)，他曾在彼得·蒂尔 (Peter Thiel) 的 Clarium Capital 工作。 最终，简街公司（包括山姆·班克曼-弗里德在内的年轻有效利他主义者加入的华尔街公司）也加入了进来。 “Jane Street 在态势感知方面的投资尤其引人注目，因为该公司很少将资金分配给外部基金经理，”《华尔街日报》六月写道。

为什么这些自称严肃​​的人会购买一个 24 岁年轻人的第一支对冲基金？ 我最好的猜测是，阿申布伦纳的投资者依赖的是他培养的社会诚意。 社会证明是审查人们的最懒惰和最灾难性的方式——问问任何 Theranos 投资者，或者任何让伯尼·麦道夫 (Bernie Madoff) 管理资金的人——但我认为这对于硅谷来说已经足够好了。

17岁时，阿申布伦纳被硅谷某些圈子里著名的自由主义经济学家泰勒·考恩称为“经济学神童”。 据《财富》杂志报道，考恩的 Emergent Ventures 甚至给了他一笔资助。 阿申布伦纳在 Stripe 资助的出版物 Works in Progress 上发表了论文。 在哥伦比亚大学期间，阿申布伦纳与他人共同创立了该学院的有效利他主义分会。 2021 年，19 岁的阿申布伦纳 (Aschenbrenner) 作为哥伦比亚大学的告别演说者毕业后，继续在 FTX 未来基金工作，该基金是加密货币交易所 FTX 的慈善部门，在 Sam Bankman-Fried 的欺诈行为被揭露后，该基金倒闭了。 他在该基金的同事中有有效利他主义运动的哲学家国王威廉·麦克阿斯基尔（William MacAskill）和后来成为人类基金会（Anthropic）幕僚长的阿维塔尔·巴尔维特（Avital Balwit）。

从那时起，他立即在 OpenAI 的超级对齐团队中找到了一份工作。 《财富》杂志援引几位前同事的话说，他“政治上笨拙”、傲慢且粗鲁。 “多名研究人员还描述了一次假日聚会，在一次随意的小组讨论中，阿申布伦纳告诉当时的 Scale AI 首席执行官 Alexandr Wang OpenAI 有多少 GPU——正如有人所说，‘直接公开’，”《财富》杂志的 Sharon Goldman 在她的个人资料中写道。 （王和阿申布伦纳都否认发生过这种情况。） Aschenbrenner 后来因在与 Scale AI 事件无关的事件中泄露内部信息而被 OpenAI 解雇。 两个月后，阿申布伦纳发表了他的论文《态势感知》。

“显然，不爆炸是第一和第二项任务。”

现在，精明的读者可能会注意到，阿申布伦纳在创办对冲基金时，他的简历上并没有任何资金管理经验。 他们可能还注意到，Aschenbrenner 的工作经验总计在 FTX 工作了几个月，在 OpenAI 工作了大约一年。 他们可能会想，如果科里森一家、格罗斯一家和弗里德曼一家为这个小玩意提供资金，这是否意味着他们有太多的钱可以烧了。 （是的，显然。 向富人征税！）

阿申布伦纳 (Aschenbrenner) 是这样描述该基金在 2024 年太平日子里的策略的：“显然，不崩溃是第一和第二项任务，”他告诉帕特尔。 “你必须把握好时机。 通往 AGI 之路的押注顺序实际上非常关键。 人们低估了它。”

在接下来的几天里，我们将更全面地了解态势感知是如何崩溃和燃烧的，但现在看起来是这样的。 对冲基金经常借钱来最大化他们的赌注。 因此，如果你真的相信人工智能是未来，“你就不会将 100% 的资金（以及投资者的资金）投入到人工智能的繁荣中，”彭博社的马特·莱文 (Matt Levine) 写道。 “你会把 300% 的钱投入到人工智能的繁荣中。” 该对冲基金一度声称股价上涨了 439%。

同样的借贷会放大你的盈利，也会放大你的亏损。 如果你借钱押注人工智能股票，而这些股票下跌（就像最近发生的那样），向你借钱的人会进行所谓的“追加保证金通知”，并要求你补充贷款抵押品。 据英国《金融时报》昨天报道，首先，态势感知公司与其投资者和贷方举行了电话会议，以筹集更多资金。 它甚至为一些投资者提供了购买部分投资组合的机会。 今天早上，Situational Awareness 将英国《金融时报》所说的“其 160 亿美元公共股权的很大一部分”出售给了格里芬的对冲基金 Citadel。

“你必须非常非常小心你的整体风险定位。”

公共股权是任何人投资组合中流动性最强的部分。 据英国《金融时报》报道，Situational Awareness 仍拥有私人股份，其中包括价值 50 亿美元的 Anthropic。 据 CNBC 报道，态势感知公司也在就出售该股份进行谈判，“但尚不清楚这笔交易是否已完成。”

阿申布伦纳 (Aschenbrenner) 在 2024 年表示：“你必须对整体风险定位非常非常谨慎。” “如果你预计这些疯狂的事件会发生，那么就会出现你没有预见到的疯狂的事情。” 其中之一也许是通用人工智能不会到来——或者至少不会在 2027 年到来。 “一位朋友开玩笑说，这家投资公司对我来说是完美的对冲，”阿申布伦纳说。 “要么AGI在这十年发生，我的人力资本贬值，但我把它变成金融资本，要么没有AGI发生，公司表现不好，但我仍然二十多岁，很聪明。”

是的，阿申布伦纳肯定已经 20 多岁了！
